4 NOTE: To determine the appropriate reset procedure, refer to TPMS REMINDER RESET INDEX . Only vehicles listed in this index have a TPMS reset.

CAUTION: 1st generation TPM wheel electronics are not compatible with 2nd generation TPM wheel electronics. 1st generation is up to 2008, and 2nd generation is 2009 and beyond.

If wheels with wheel electronics from the 1st TPM generation are mounted on a vehicle with a 2nd generation TPM system (or vice versa), the wheel electronics will not be recognized by the TPM system. The TPM system is not active and a corresponding warning is displayed in the multi-function display of the instrument cluster. The wheel electronics will also be stored as defective in the fault memory of the TPM control unit.

Wheel electronics unit (sensor) part numbers are: • 2005-07: 997.606.021.00 433MHz) • 2008: 997.606.021.01 (433 MHz) • 2009-: 997.606.021.20 (433 MHz)

Tire Pressure Monitoring begins to "learn" the wheels after a wheel change, wheel transmiter replacement, a tire pressure adjustment (when a warning message has been displayed), once an update of the tire settings has been performed. During this process, Tire Pressure Monitoring recognizes the wheels and their locations. The message "No monitoring, system is learning" appears on the multipurpose display. The wheel learning process takes place exclusively when the vehicle is being driven above 16 mph (25 km/h). Tire Pressure Monitoring requires a certain amount of time to learn the wheels.

. NOTE: The tire type and size must be updated even if the settings for the new set of wheels are the same as for the old wheels. If the tire setings are not updated, the message "TIRE CHANGE? UPDATE SETTINGS!" is displayed on the multi-purpose display.

1. Select menu "TYRE PRESSURE", "SETTINGS, then "TYRES". Set tire type and tire size (both items must be set).

o NOTE: The tire type and size must be selected even if the settings for the new set of wheels are the same as for the old wheels.

2. The learning process is now started, and wilbe completed when vehicle is driven. The message "NO MONITORING - SYSTEM LEARNING" is displayed. The current tire pressure will not be displayed until the learning phase is complete.

When the vehicle is stationary after a tire pressure warning, the screen changes to "SELECTION AFTER WARNING". See Fig 1. Choose the appropriate procedure:

If tire pressure was changed, see Adding Air .   
If a wheel was changed, see Wheel Change .   
If a flat is repaired using tire sealant, see Sealing Set .

NOTE: If a selection is made in the "SELECTION AFTER WARNING" display without performing the appropriate actions, the message "CAUTION - FLAT TYRE - CHECK TYRES" will be displayed.

D ADD AIR WHEELCHANGE SEALING SET G00225546 Омрн

1. Select "WHEEL CHANGE" from "SELECTION AFTER WARNING" menu. The display will return to "SPARE WHEEL" menu after acknowledgement. Select spare wheel type.

2. If the tire type and size of the new tires have not been set , a "WHEEL CHANGE? CHECK SETTINGS" message will be displayed. When vehicle is stopped, display will return to "SELECTION AFTER WARNING" menu. Perform previous step.

Radial and lateral runout of the rim and/or rim/tire assembly.

Flat spots can occur on the tires if the vehicle is idle for extended periods.

WM 440593 BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS (ALL MODELS) > BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS > EXPLANATION OF TERMS > RADIAL FORCE VARIATIONS

![](images/_MISSING_ca43932fc425b45d567be8ac9345be0eb6bc7c5ec5b0d19e2f10f777763d6eef.jpg)  
Fig 1: Identifying Rim/Tire Assembly Radial And Lateral Runout

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

The radial force is a force that compresses a tire. Based on its size, a tire has softer (-item A- ) and more rigid zones (-item B- ) due to constructive and production-related factors. Given this, the tire compresses to various extents at a constant wheel load (-arrow 1- ) and a constant tire pressure (-arrows 2- ). This varying spring action (-X- ) in the tire can cause vibrations in the chassis on even road surfaces and the driver may notice this as shaking in the steering wheel, for example. Measuring the radial force variation involves running the tire on a wheel balancer that measures radial force variation while applying a constant load to the tire. This simulates the rolling of the tire on a driving surface. Variations in radial force occur independently of the direction of rotation of the tire and are measured as the difference between the maximum and minimum radial force ("peak-to-peak" value).

The changes in radial force variation can be broken down mathematicall into individual variations. Porsche uses the value of the 1st Harmonic Variation (basic variation) to assess the tire from the point of view of rigidity. The 1st Harmonic Variation relates to the changes in radial force that cause the strongest vibrations. Changes in radial force can also result in further harmonic variations (2nd-4th Harmonic). These relate to the changes in radial force that cause weaker vibrations.

### WM 440593 BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS (ALL MODELS) > BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS


Turn the tire on the wheel by 90° or 180° if necessary in order to achieve an acceptable value with regard to rolling smoothness (true running, imbalance and distribution of balance weights).

This is the filing pressure after the tire has been fitted on the rim at which the tire bead, coming out of the deep bed, must pop over the hump of the rim bead. This seating pressure must not exceed 4 bar.

In certain cases, it may be necessary to measure radial force variations. This should be done before normal balancing is performed.

The entire process is subdivided into several operations:

1. Fitting the tire on the rim.

2.2.

A. Measuring radial force variations and optimizing the wheels if necessary. Then balancing the wheels.   
B. As an alternative to item 2 A, if there is no device available to measure radial force variations: Stationary balancing of the wheel (eliminating static and dynamic imbalance) with optimization of rolling smoothness.

3. Fitting the wheel on the vehicle.

oRemove rubber residues and dried-on tire paste from the rim, especially from the rim bead and the hump.   
Check rim for damage; remove old balancing weights.   
o Use the specified tire mounting pastes Remaxx Sport mounting paste (from Rema Tip Top/Item No. 593 0577) or Bead Lubricant (from Rema Tip Top/Item No. 514 4985) or Gleitmittel VA sliding compound (from Azett/Item No. 5000-021-220) so that the tire does not turn on the rim - undoing all your careful work - the first time you drive the vehicle. If the tire turns by as litle as 20 mm with respect to the rim, this can worsen an optimum balancing result.   
o Fit tire on the rim. When doing so, it is a good idea - and even necessary in some cases - to fit the tire at a favorable position with respect to the rim (matching). Compare Controlled and Uncontrolled matching below.

oTension wheel on balancing machine with radial force variation measurement (vibration monitoring system).   
oObserve the operating instructions of the balancing machine (adjust the machine from time to time).   
oThe contact surface of the wheel on the balancing flange (flat surface) and the centering surface must be clean.   
oThe display disabling function must be switched off.   
oAdjust tire pressure to 2.7 bar (best test pressure) when balancing and measuring radial force variations.   
oParticular attention must be paid to the wheel mounting when measuring radial force variations and when balancing. Using the special pressure pieces provided by the manufacturer of the balancing machine wil ensure that wheels are balanced accurately and there is the highest possible repeat accuracy. Read the operating instructions.

This can happen if the tire mounting paste is not completely dry. Optimum balancing will be impaired as a result.

Observe the following criteria during the test drive:

1.7.1. TPM function (tire Pressure Monitoring system).

Before starting the test drive (with "ignition on'"), select the mounted set of wheels under Main menu > tire pressure > Settings in the instrument cluster. The control unit then learns the wheel positions again while the vehicle is driving.

The system starts learning as soon as you accelerate above 25 km/h (16 mph). The learning time is normally about 30 seconds, but can take several minutes when the vehicle is driven in a metallic environment (e.g. multi-storey car park, bridge and other concrete, highly metallic surfaces).

2. 7.2. Rough running performance and vibrations

Tires must be stored in a cool, dry and dark room with adequate ventilation. They must never come into contact with fuel, oil, grease or chemicals. Complete wheels can be stacked for storage. It is advisable to increase the tire pressure by 0.4 bar (6 psi).

If the tires are not mounted on wheels, store them in the vertical position. Tires stored in vertical position should be turned every two weeks in order to prevent excessive flat spots. If the tires are stacked in horizontal position, they will become severely deformed and cannot be seated in the rim flange easily when mounted.

Tires age due to physical and chemical processes, which can impair their function. If they are stored for an extended period, they wil harden and become brittle faster than tires that are in continual use. Hairline ageing cracks can occur on older tires. If tires are in use, the kneading action activates the plasticizer in the rubber and thereby prevents hardening and cracking.

### WM 4495TW CONVERSION TABLE FOR WHEEL ALIGNMENT VALUES (ALL MODELS) > MINUTES TO 


1. To check the height, position ready-to-drive vehicle (fully tanked with tire repair kit or spare wheel and tools) on a flat surface or on the measuring station. The normal vehicle level must be set for vehicles with air suspension. Please read the section: Special notes for vehicles with air suspension

2. On vehicles with air suspension/levelling system, switch off the levelling system (and switch it back on again when work is complete).

1.2.1. Use PIWis Tester Il 9818 to select >>Levelling system/PASM<< >>Drive links/checks<< >>Activate/deactivate vehicle<< in the control unit overview.

2. 2.2. Select the value Deactivate levelling system (permanently) and press [F8] to start. The levelling system is now switched off.

3. Compress vehicle at front and rear axles by approximately 25 mm 2-3 times and allow it to spring back freely.

4. Open the bonnet.

5. Measure the vehicle height -dimension 1- at all four wheels on the vehicle.

Fig 1: Identifying Wheel To Wing Lower Edge Dimension (Rear Axle)

![](images/_MISSING_aa380a92f8d9aea17af3b3cb78447be1d0e792b662f76a4be0a6b959f8785040.jpg)

Toe difference angle and caster cannot be adjusted.   
Camber at the front axle cannot be adjusted. But camber can be centered evenly within the tolerance range by moving the front-axle carrier. 1. Prepare vehicle for checking and/or adjusting wheel alignment values. Place front wheels on

turntable and rear wheels on rotary/sliding plates.

2. Compress vehicle as far as possible (by a few mm) at front and rear axles twice or three times and allow it to spring back freely.

Information

The wheel alignment values are specified in degrees and minutes in the Technical Manual (division in 60 units).   
In countries in which the decimal degree is widely used, the electronic wheel alignment testers can be converted from degrees/minutes (division in 60 units) to decimal degrees (division in 100 units) by pressing a key (special function). This function is standard for the electronic wheel alignment testers approved by Porsche.   
Minutes (') can be converted into decimal degrees and decimal degrees into minutes (') using the conversion table. To do this, read out the required values from the table using the co-ordinates.

![](images/_MISSING_bb657e4609bafc3f8c292b49e357ed01e446ea984e3ded3335dde29248357fbb.jpg)

Example 1: toe 17 min (17') = 0.283 decimal degrees according to table. Procedure for this: The imaginary line starting at the top of the 7-min column moving downwards and the line starting on the left in the 10-min row moving right meet at point/column 0.283.

Example 2: camber 1° 25' (1 degree and 25 min) = 1.417 decimal degrees. This is the result from the table (1 degree or 60 min) = 1.000 + 0.417 (25 min).

Example 1: toe 0.350 decimal degree = 21 min (21'). A search is performed for the decimal value (0.350) in the table. The co-ordinates are then formed from this point/value. Line to the left = 20' and line upwards = 1' (which equals 20' + 1').

Example 2: camber 1.683 decimal degrees = 1° 41' (1 degree and 41 min). This result is obtained as follows: Split the value into 1.000 = 1 degree (1°) and search for the remainder 0.683 in the table. Then form the co-ordinates again. Line to the left = 40' and line upwards = 1' (which equals

40' + 1').

4. Heating

If the damage is more severe, the removal of trapped air can be speeded up by heating the area gently. To do this, use a lighter to heat the area of damage from the inside for 3-5 seconds.

0 IMPORTANT: Heat during the vacuum phase only, otherwise the expanding air would cause excessive pressure in the damaged area.

The dent must not have any cracks in the paintwork. Examine the damaged area using an illuminated magnifier or reflected-light microscope.   
Measure thickness of paint layer around the damaged area. Paint layers up to approx. 450 μm thick are straightforward. With thicker layers of paint there is a danger that the paint will crack.

### WM 503819 REMOVING AND INSTALLING LOCK CARRIER SIDE SECTION AT THE LEFT (ALL MOD


The factors below affect the outcome of the repair work considerably:

The location of the damage   
The extent of the damage   
The shape of the damage   
The condition of the paintwork   
Skills and experience of the technician   
Color (dark colors are trickier than light colors)   
With silver colors, sharp-edged and pointed dents may cause slight changes to the color pigments (dark sports).   
Condition of tools

With the clock method, the lines of force running through the center of the dent are removed, with the result that the material stress is reduced and the panel is flat again.

The dent should be envisaged as a dial with "12" being the furthest away. In other words, the person performing the work is standing at 6 o'clock.

Start at the edge of the dent -A- at 9 o'clock and work clockwise through 12 o'clock to 3 o'clock. When doing this, always remember to press the panel at as many points as possible and as close together as possible. From 3 o'clock, move further inwards and carry on through 12 o'clock to 9 o'clock. Carry out the remaining steps in this same way.

![](images/_MISSING_b5f0a8b8597cddb871f2d49d67d0875412f6a7a4d5f9da00b5f37a12e0cf13b4.jpg)  
Fig 1: Identifying Dent Repair Clock Method   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

With a dent of approx. 2 cm in diameter, it will be necessary to press the panel at around 100 - 150 points. Any point that is pressed too hard must be pushed back again before continuing. Strain can be created in the panel as a result of too many high points, with the result that the metal sheet can no longer spread out evenly.

### WM 5XOOIN SAFETY NOTES (ALL MODELS) > SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR ADHESIVE BONDING >


![](images/_MISSING_d4656d9e8201d342e21f66da6d7d3958b19059bdf1c98c4baf0780e1a1723ff8.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_b45bc8cf321797b09d6f5c62e330777ab645a9352e39c76e56ba381363cff0d0.jpg)

WARNiNG: Excessively high dust concentration during grinding work

Risk of explosion

→ Remove any grinding dust using the relevant vacuum cleaner approved for use on the material.

→ Remove dust in the work area regularly.

→ Do not use compressed air to blow away dust deposits.

→ Always separate the dust from different materials (separate aluminum, steel and carbon fibrereinforced plastic).

→ Clean the extraction system at regular intervals.   
→ Never weld and grind in the same room at the same time.   
→ Only use pneumatic grinders if possible.

WARNING: Grinding and welding work

Danger of fire or explosion

→ Avoid working in an area with highly inflammable or explosive materials.

→ Cover highly inflammable or explosive areas.

→ Remove highly inflammable or explosive parts.

WARNING: Toxic substances

• Danger of poisoning or suffocation Danger of burns to the eyes and skin

→ Ventilate the work area well.

→ Never ingest or inhale.

→ Read specific information on the Hazard Sheet.

→ Do not smoke, eat or drink in the work area.

NOTE: Non-observance of setting time for adhesive

Risk of damage to side panel

→ Weld in the new part within 30 minutes.

•Cartridge and ambient temperature: -40 - 90 °C • Optimal temperature: 20 - 30 °C

Small amounts remaining after mixing and complete hardening may be disposed of as industrial waste.

Dispose of used acetone-soaked cleaning cloths as special-category waste.

### WM 631719 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT RETAINING STRIP (ALL MODELS) > INSTALLIN

NOTE: Replacing the hydraulic unit/control unit

•The hydraulic unit forms a single unit with the control unit.   
The hydraulic unit and control unit are always replaced together.   
When replacing the hydraulic unit/control unit, the new assembly must be to hand before the old one is removed.   
•The data as well as the coding of the old control unit must be transferred to the new unit before the old one is removed.

→ When replacing, note the following: —→ 453055 REPLACING HYDRAULIC UNIT/CONTROL UNIT .

NOTE: Dirt on injection system components

Material damage • Rough-running engine Bad exhaust emissions

→ Thoroughly clean connection points and adjacent areas before loosening them. If the engine is very dirty, wash it before starting disassembly work.

→ Lay removed parts on a clean surface and cover them. Do not use fibre-shedding cloths.

→ Carefully cover components or seal them if repair work will not be carried out immediately. Place rubber caps on connections. Seal intake openings with film or adhesive tape.

→ Only installclean parts. Do not take spare parts out of the packaging until just before installtion.   
→ Never use compressed air when the system is open. Do not move the vehicle.

### CALIFORNIA > PASS/FAIL EMISSION STANDARDS = A+B / VTW


ESC - Emission Standard Category

GVWR - Manufacture's Gross Vehicle Weight Rating

LVW - Loaded Vehicle Weight

PC - Passenger Car

LDT1 - Light-Duty Truck up through 3750 LVW and GVWR no greater than 6000 Ibs.

LDT2 - Light-Duty Truck greater than 3750 LVW and GVWR no greater than 6000 Ibs.

MDV - Medium-Duty Vehicle, GVWR from 6001 to 8500 Ibs.

HC - Hydrocarbon, ppm

CO - Carbon Monoxide, %

NO - Nitric Oxide, ppm

PASS/FAIL STANDARDS - Emission standards used to determine if a vehicle passes the emission inspection. A vehicle passes if the emission levels are equal to or less than the standards for HC, CO and NO for ASM 5015 and ASM 2525.

GROSS POLLUTER STANDARDS - Emission standards used to designate a vehicle as a gross polluter A vehicle is designated as a gross polluter if the emission levels at the time of the initial inspection, before repairs are greater than the gross poluter standards for HC, CO or NO for ASM 5015 or ASM 2525.

NOTE: If test data on emission pass/fail rates or gross polluter identification rates indicate adjustments are required, the emission standards may be increased or decreased by the bureau by 30% or by the following tolerances, or standards may be set for any specific vehicle and engine configuration which the bureau determines has excessive errors of commission of omission, whichever is necessary to comply with Section 44001.5 of the Health and Safety Code.

### WM 825919 REMOVING AND INSTALLING MUFFLER (SILENCER) (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING AND


Install glove compartment → INSTALLING GLOVE COMPARTMENT .

![](images/_MISSING_5223299be6045641643d051960f9b686862cab7b5e7cbc3a9ff64148a8b2e82f.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_f303660db85ef3a8dd5cd71e09db879f3c278a1ed377dfc8d45adbbfcd18e053.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_8f99954010f82805c414aaeae04919d76a7d6c08e7348803b65cb991ebee96da.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_f60827bb05c4a9d145a91556705e63d9e62a12afb56971f7e560a22156246ed5.jpg)

1. Position silencer.

.Tighten fastening nut -3- on the silencer holder to the prescribed tightening torque Tightening torque 9 Nm (6.5 ftlb.) .

![](images/_MISSING_b930da5288fb357c50093a8eca433780670f845cf33b220b101bf79d95b7b2b2.jpg)  
Fig 1: Identifying Silencer Holder

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Tighten fastening nut -1- at the bottom of the wheel housing to the prescribed tightening torque Tightening torque 9 Nm (6.5 ftlb.) .

![](images/_MISSING_06b1a5569ca810d0eae7157f76a32ddb0081ff60b3b4655c79242915dbac9232.jpg)  
Fig 2: Identifying Silencer On Underbody

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Secure line -1- to the silencer holder -2- .

5. Slide flexi-pipe -2- onto the silencer pipe -3- .

![](images/_MISSING_20301f87163bccaab7816f6155b0fab6383bae1e6338ebe3ba41d8531b9545e3.jpg)  
Fig 3: Identifying Silencer Holder

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

6. Tighten screw-type clamp -1- .

![](images/_MISSING_5a351027a17c3bd2cf87a7a8a900f63155969aef5c7bece38adb44eaad900d72.jpg)  
Fig 4: Identifying Exhaust Pipe On Silencer

1. Refrigerant circuit is open for > 20 minutes.

Amount of refrigerant extracted is < 30% of the required quantity.

3. Refrigerant circuit has been open for an indefinite period of time (gradual leak, stone damage to condenser).

4. Air-conditioning compressor has become blocked.

5. Dryer cartridge is damaged.

6. After opening the packaging and line connections (on a new desiccator), the desiccator must be installed within 20 minutes at the latest and the refrigerant circuit must be closed, evacuated and filled.

1. If the components are closed off using stoppers immediately after opening the refrigerant circuit and the refrigerant circuit is closed and evacuated within 20 minutes at the latest.

1.4.1. Before closing off the refrigerant circuit, check whether the desiccator needs to be replaced.

2.4.2. If necessary, reconnect high-pressure and low-pressure lines.

5. Evacuate the system and check for leaks.

1. 5.1. If the air-conditioning system has been opened, evacuation should last at least 20 minutes so that the moisture can evaporate and be removed by suction.

2. 5.2. If the air-conditioning system has been open for a long time, evacuation can be carried out for up to 120 minutes.

3. 5.3. Check the pressure gauge for approx. 2 minutes. If the pressure rises, air is entering the vehicle's air-conditioning system. The leak must be located and repaired.

If the pressure remains constant, add refrigerant oil.

9. Add refrigerant from both connection hoses to the air-conditioning system in the vehicle.

1.9.1. The refrigerant in the high-pressure and low-pressure lines is part of the filing capacity of the refrigerant in the air-conditioning system in the vehicle.

2.9.2. Close the valve on the high-pressure line and disconnect it from the vehicle.

3.9.3. Start the engine and air-conditioning system. When the pressure on both pressure gauges falls below 2 bar, close the valve on the low-pressure line and disconnect it from the vehicle.

1. Drain refrigerant → 870317 DRAINING AND FILLING REFRIGERANT .

7. Remove reservoir (do not open hydraulic system!) → 194019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING RESERVOIR

Danger of poisoning or suffocation •Danger of burns to the eyes and skin

→ Ventilate the work area well.

The refrigerant circuit of the air-conditioning system may only be emptied and opened if this is necessary in order to comply with safety measures or if components of the refrigerant circuit have to be replaced.

The air-conditioning refrigerant circuit also remains closed during all other standard vehicle repair work

For this reason, the manufacturer only fits connecting elements with a special surface coating.

Contact corrosion can occur if unsuitable connecting elements (screws, nuts, washers, rivets, plugs, adhesives, etc.) are used.

Only use original Porsche parts!

1. Move selector lever from position "P" to "D" and from position "D" to "M" and back again several times.

.Check that the parking lock is disengaged.

1.2.1. Insert ignition key into the ignition lock.

2. 2.2. Move selector lever to position "P". "P" appears in the instrument cluster.

3.2.3. Actuate the service brake.

4.2.4. Start the engine.

5. 2.5. Move selector lever to position "D". "D" appears in the instrument cluster.

6.2.6. Release the service brake. If the vehicle moves forward, the test is complete. Otherwise, all connecting pieces must be checked again.

3. Check that the parking lock is engaged (engine running).

1.3.1. Insert ignition key into the ignition lock.

2. 3.2. Move selector lever to position "P". "P" appears in the instrument cluster.

3.3.3. Actuate the service brake.

4.3.4. Start the engine.

5. 3.5. Release the service brake. The vehicle must not move. Otherwise, the entire system must be checked.

6.3.6. Switch off engine.

4.Check that the parking lock is engaged (blocking effect).

1.4.1. Insert ignition key into the ignition lock.

2. 4.2. Move selector lever to position "P". "P" appears in the instrument cluster.

3. 4.3. Move selector lever to position "N". "N" appears in the instrument cluster.

4. 4.4. Get another person to help you to push the vehicle for a distance of at least one metre. It must be possible to move the vehicle. Otherwise, the entire system must be checked.

5.4.5. Actuate the service brake.

6. 4.6. Move selector lever to position "P". "P" appears in the instrument cluster.

7. 4.7. Get another person to help you to push the vehicle. The vehicle must not move (a max. movement of 150 mm is acceptable). Otherwise, the entire system must be checked.

1. On the PIWiS Tester start screen, call up the ==> 'Diagnostics' menu and select the relevant vehicle type.

The diagnostic application is then started and the control unit selection screen is populated.

2. Select the control unit to be programmed in the control unit selection screen (==> "Overview" menu) and press [>] to confirm your selection → see Fig 1.

![](images/_MISSING_a50dffae6fd9afcec9ed443ce91363714e83cab22306c7b4dfaafc837a386a26.jpg)  
Fig 1: Screen Display - Control Unit Selection

3. When the question "Create Vehicle Analysis Log (VAL)?" appears, either press [F12] to create a VAL or press [F11] if you do not want to create a VAL.

4. Press [>] to acknowledge the message that may appear informing you that campaigns for the vehicle are stored in the PIWIS information system.

5. Once the control unit to be programmed has been found, select the ==> 'Programming' menu

6. Select the ==> 'Automatic programming'function and press [>>] to confirm your selection and start the guided programming sequence → see Fig 2.

During the programming sequence, the control unit is re-programmed and then re-coded automatically if necessary.

### WM 9XOOIN BASIC INSTRUCTIONS AND PROCEDURE FOR CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING USING TH


1. On the PlWis Tester start screen, call up the ==> 'Diagnostics' menu and select the relevant vehicle type.

The diagnostic application is then started and the control unit selection screen is populated.

2. In the control unit selection screen ("Overview" menu), press [F7] to callup the ==> 'Additional menu' (→ see Fig 1).

![](images/_MISSING_c9f62cc2564b4ddd873b9165f14fe5d565dfabd40a4a304c651569defc707205.jpg)  
Fig 1: Screen Display - Control Unit Selection

3. When the question "Create Vehicle Analysis Log (VAL)?" appears, either press [>] to create a

VAL or press [F11] if you do not want to create a VAL.

4. Press [>] to acknowledge the message that may appear informing you that campaigns for the vehicle are stored in the PIWiS information system.

5. Select the ==> 'Campaign' function and press [>>] to confirm your selection → see Fig 2. You are then prompted to enter a programming code.

![](images/_MISSING_c30793a51886d04a656b32f048244a166b29e77df08d05ba80ee9b99f770bbe6.jpg)  
Fig 2: Screen Display - Additional Menu - Campaign

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

6. To enter the programming code, click in the relevant text box so that the cursor starts to flash → see Fig 3.

![](images/_MISSING_bf019aaf6006c51bb934a2a69976c5b5c21afe50f1bfb7e35d7e50aa194e0f6c.jpg)  
Fig 3: Screen Display - Programming Code Input Field

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Enter the programming code specified in the relevant description (Technical Information, Service Information) and press Enter to confirm your entry.

The text box turns blue.

8. Press [>>] to start the guided programming sequence.

Read and follow the information and instructions on the Piwis Tester during the guided programming sequence. Then press [>>] to continue.

During the programming sequence, the control unit is re-programmed and then re-coded automatically if necessary.

1. Select menu "TIRE PRESSURE", then "ADJUST". Set tire type and tire size (both items must be set). See Operating Multi-Purpose Display .

9 NOTE: If tires have been rotated, tire pressure changed, or a tire pressure sensor or wheel has been replaced, the TPM system must be reset. See Tire Pressure Monitor System Reset . When vehicle is stationary after a tire pressure warning, the display changes to "SELECTION AFTER WARNING" screen. See "Selection After Warning" Reset .

If tire pressures have been adjusted, without being prompted by a TPMS warning indicator, no reset procedure is required. ftire pressures have been adjusted after a TPMS warning indicator display, see "Selection After Warning" Reset .

1. After inflating the wheel in question, select "ADD AIR" from "SELECTION AFTER WARNING" menu. The display will return to the basic screen after acknowledgement.

2. If vehicle is driven without selecting "ADD AIR", a "WHEN VEHICLE STOPS: HIT SELECTION" message will be displayed. When vehicle is stopped, perform previous step.

After repairing flat tire with tire sealant, select "SEALING SET". The display wil return to the basic screen after acknowledgement. A warning message will display if vehicle speed exceeds 50 mph (80 km/h).

5. Select Instrument cluster control unit, then press [>].

3.11.3. Switch on ignition.

→ Only install clean parts. Do not take spare parts out of the packaging until just before installtion.

→ Never use compressed air when the system is open. Do not move the vehicle.

The height measurement shows that front left vehicle height is 430 mm and the measured value is not accepted during height sensor calibration.

Actual value: 430 mm; required value: 464 mm

(Actual value + required value)/2 = mean value

(430 mm + 464 mm)/2 = 447 mm

Now enter the value 447 mm for the front left height in the Porsche System Tester.
